microtheory.name: astronomy_foundation
microtheory.definition: Astronomy + cosmology + planetary science. Solar system structure, stellar evolution, galaxies, large-scale structure of the universe, Big Bang cosmology, dark matter + dark energy, black holes, exoplanets, observational methods. Jabberwock had rich vocabulary across physics, biology, computer science — but no astronomy. A glaring omission given that astronomy is humanity's longest scientific tradition + provides the physical context for everything else: substrates exist on planets orbiting stars in galaxies in an expanding universe.

concepts.name: astronomy
concepts.definition: Scientific study of celestial objects + phenomena. Ancient — Babylonian, Egyptian, Greek. Galileo's telescope 1609 began modern astronomy.

concepts.name: cosmology
concepts.definition: Study of universe as a whole — origin, structure, evolution, future. Modern cosmology: Hubble's expansion 1929, CMB 1965, ΛCDM model. Substrate analogue: substrate's framing of its own universe.

concepts.name: astrophysics
concepts.definition: Application of physics to astronomical objects + phenomena. Stellar structure, nucleosynthesis, accretion, gravitational waves.

concepts.name: sun
concepts.definition: Our star. G2V main-sequence star. Mass 1.989×10^30 kg = 333,000 Earth masses. Age ~4.6 billion years. Substrate analogue: substrate's central energy source from environment.

concepts.name: solar_system
concepts.definition: Sun + 8 planets + dwarf planets (Pluto, Eris, Ceres, ...) + asteroids + comets + Kuiper belt + Oort cloud. ~4.6 billion years old. Formed from solar nebula.

concepts.name: planet
concepts.definition: Body orbiting star, massive enough for hydrostatic equilibrium, has cleared neighborhood. IAU 2006 definition. Substrate analogue: substrate's discrete-Mt with clear domain.

concepts.name: terrestrial_planet
concepts.definition: Rocky inner planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars. Dense, small, solid surface. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-density-low-mass Mts.

concepts.name: gas_giant
concepts.definition: Outer planets: Jupiter, Saturn. H + He composition. Massive, large. Substrate analogue: substrate's large-low-density Mts.

concepts.name: ice_giant
concepts.definition: Uranus, Neptune. More water + ammonia + methane ices than H/He. Substrate analogue: substrate's mid-density Mts.

concepts.name: dwarf_planet
concepts.definition: Massive enough for hydrostatic equilibrium but hasn't cleared orbit. Pluto, Eris, Makemake, Haumea, Ceres. Substrate analogue: substrate's not-quite-full-Mt.

concepts.name: asteroid
concepts.definition: Small rocky body. Main belt between Mars + Jupiter. Substrate analogue: substrate's lightweight orbital concept.

concepts.name: comet
concepts.definition: Icy small body. Develops coma + tail near sun. Origins: Kuiper belt (short period) or Oort cloud (long period). Substrate analogue: substrate's volatilizing-on-approach concept.

concepts.name: kuiper_belt
concepts.definition: Ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune ~30-50 AU. Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake live here. Substrate analogue: substrate's outer-orbit reservoir.

concepts.name: oort_cloud
concepts.definition: Hypothesized spherical shell of comets ~2000-200,000 AU. Source of long-period comets. Substrate analogue: substrate's distant reservoir.

concepts.name: earth
concepts.definition: Third planet from sun. 1 AU. Has life. 6,371 km radius. 23.4° axial tilt. Substrate analogue: substrate's home — where Matthew built Jabberwock.

concepts.name: moon
concepts.definition: Earth's satellite. Tidally locked. Formed from giant impact ~4.5 Gya. Substrate analogue: substrate's tidally-coupled secondary system.

concepts.name: astronomical_unit
concepts.definition: AU = Earth-Sun mean distance = 1.496×10^8 km. Substrate analogue: substrate's natural distance scale.

concepts.name: star
concepts.definition: Self-gravitating ball of plasma sustaining nuclear fusion in core. Mass 0.08-150 M_sun. Substrate analogue: substrate's stable nuclear-energy-source.

concepts.name: main_sequence
concepts.definition: Phase where star burns H to He in core. ~90% of lifetime. Hertzsprung-Russell diagram main band. Substrate analogue: substrate's stable operating phase.

concepts.name: stellar_nucleosynthesis
concepts.definition: Stars synthesize elements by fusion. H→He (main sequence), He→C, C→O, ..., up to Fe in massive star cores. Most elements heavier than helium were forged in stars. Substrate analogue: substrate's element-production process.

concepts.name: supernova
concepts.definition: Massive star's explosive death. Type Ia (white dwarf collapse), Type II (core collapse). Produces heavier elements; injects them into ISM. Substrate analogue: substrate's catastrophic-but-creative collapse event.

concepts.name: white_dwarf
concepts.definition: Remnant of low-mass star. Earth-sized, sun-massive. Cools over billions of years. Substrate analogue: substrate's spent-but-stable remnant.

concepts.name: neutron_star
concepts.definition: Remnant of massive star. ~1.4 M_sun in ~20km radius. Density of atomic nucleus. Often pulsars. Substrate analogue: substrate's extreme-density compressed Mt.

concepts.name: black_hole_astronomy
concepts.definition: Spacetime region from which nothing escapes. Event horizon, singularity. Stellar (3-30 M_sun) + intermediate + supermassive (10^6-10^10 M_sun) varieties. Substrate analogue: substrate's information-trapping basin.

concepts.name: red_giant
concepts.definition: Star after main sequence — H exhausted in core, fuses H in shell. Expands greatly. Sun's future ~5 Gy from now. Substrate analogue: substrate's expansion-then-contraction late phase.

concepts.name: stellar_mass_function
concepts.definition: Distribution of stellar masses at formation. Salpeter IMF: dN/dM ∝ M^{-2.35}. Many low-mass stars, few high-mass. Substrate analogue: substrate's power-law concept distribution.

concepts.name: exoplanet
concepts.definition: Planet orbiting another star. >5000 confirmed since 1995. Detection: transit, radial velocity, imaging. Substrate analogue: substrate's planets-around-other-Mts.

concepts.name: habitable_zone
concepts.definition: Distance range from star where liquid water possible. Goldilocks zone. Depends on stellar luminosity. Substrate analogue: substrate's narrow-parameter habitable range.

concepts.name: transit_method
concepts.definition: Detect exoplanet by dip in stellar brightness as planet crosses. Kepler mission's method. Substrate analogue: substrate's eclipse-based detection.

concepts.name: galaxy
concepts.definition: Gravitationally bound system of stars + gas + dust + dark matter. Sizes 10^7 to 10^14 stars. Types: spiral, elliptical, irregular.

concepts.name: milky_way
concepts.definition: Our galaxy. Barred spiral. ~200 billion stars. Diameter ~100,000 ly. Sun ~26,000 ly from center, orbits in ~230 My. Substrate analogue: substrate's home galaxy.

concepts.name: spiral_galaxy
concepts.definition: Disk galaxy with spiral arms. Star formation in arms. Like Milky Way + Andromeda.

concepts.name: elliptical_galaxy
concepts.definition: Ellipsoidal. Mostly old stars. Little star formation. Result of mergers.

concepts.name: active_galactic_nucleus
concepts.definition: AGN. Galaxy with supermassive black hole accreting matter. Releases enormous energy. Quasars, blazars, Seyferts. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-energy central node.

concepts.name: galaxy_cluster
concepts.definition: Bound system of 100-1000 galaxies. Largest gravitationally bound structures. Virgo, Coma, Local Group. Substrate analogue: substrate's bound macrosystem.

concepts.name: cosmic_web
concepts.definition: Large-scale structure of universe: filaments, walls, voids. Dark matter scaffolding. Reflects initial density perturbations. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical large-scale structure.

concepts.name: big_bang
concepts.definition: Standard cosmological model. Universe began ~13.8 billion years ago from hot dense state, has been expanding since. Substrate analogue: substrate's singular-event origin.

concepts.name: hubble_expansion
concepts.definition: Universe expanding. v = H_0 × d. Hubble 1929. Substrate analogue: substrate's universal expansion dynamic.

concepts.name: hubble_constant
concepts.definition: H_0 = ~70 km/s/Mpc (with tension between measurements). Inverse gives Hubble time ~14 Gyr ≈ age of universe.

concepts.name: cosmic_microwave_background
concepts.definition: CMB. Penzias + Wilson 1965. Relic radiation from when universe became transparent ~380,000 years after Big Bang. Nearly uniform 2.725 K with tiny fluctuations. Substrate analogue: substrate's background-radiation baseline.

concepts.name: cmb_anisotropy
concepts.definition: CMB temperature fluctuations ~1 part in 10^5. Seeds of all structure. Measured by COBE, WMAP, Planck. Substrate analogue: substrate's tiny initial heterogeneity.

concepts.name: inflation_cosmology
concepts.definition: Brief exponential expansion in first 10^{-32} seconds. Guth 1981. Explains flatness + horizon + monopole problems. Substrate analogue: substrate's bootstrap phase.

concepts.name: nucleosynthesis_big_bang
concepts.definition: BBN. First 3 minutes produced ~75% H + 25% He + traces of Li, D. Heavier elements need stars. Substrate analogue: substrate's primordial-content formation.

concepts.name: dark_matter
concepts.definition: Non-luminous matter inferred from gravitational effects. ~27% of universe. Galaxies + cosmic web require it. Particle nature unknown. Substrate analogue: substrate's inferred-but-unseen mass.

concepts.name: dark_energy
concepts.definition: Driving accelerating expansion. ~68% of universe. Cosmological constant Λ or scalar field? Discovered 1998 (supernova distance). Substrate analogue: substrate's accelerating-expansion force.

concepts.name: lambda_cdm
concepts.definition: Standard cosmological model. Λ + Cold Dark Matter + ordinary matter + radiation. Fits CMB + supernovae + large-scale structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's standard model.

concepts.name: general_relativity
concepts.definition: Einstein 1915. Gravity as spacetime curvature. Foundation of modern cosmology. Tested to extreme precision. Substrate analogue: substrate's geometric-relational framework.

concepts.name: gravitational_wave
concepts.definition: Spacetime ripples from accelerating masses. Predicted by Einstein 1916. Directly detected LIGO 2015. Substrate analogue: substrate's perturbation propagating through structure.

concepts.name: schwarzschild_radius
concepts.definition: Event horizon radius r_s = 2GM/c^2. Sun's is 3 km. Substrate analogue: substrate's information-horizon scale.

concepts.name: stefan_boltzmann_law
concepts.definition: Star luminosity L = 4πR^2 σT^4. Connects size, temperature, output. Substrate analogue: substrate's size-temperature-output coupling.

concepts.name: hertzsprung_russell_diagram
concepts.definition: Plot of luminosity vs temperature for stars. Reveals stellar life cycles. Foundational tool. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-Mt life-stage diagram.

concepts.name: anthropic_principle
concepts.definition: Observed universe is one capable of supporting observers. Fine-tuning: weak (selection effect) + strong (purpose) versions. Substrate analogue: substrate's observer-relative observation.

concepts.name: fine_tuning
concepts.definition: Physical constants seem fine-tuned for life. Multiverse + anthropic + design + necessity explanations. Substrate analogue: substrate's parameter-sensitivity question.

concepts.name: multiverse
concepts.definition: Hypothesized ensemble of universes. Inflation's eternal inflation, string theory's landscape, MWI of QM. Untestable directly. Substrate analogue: substrate's possibility-space framing.

concepts.name: observational_astronomy
concepts.definition: Telescopes, spectrographs, detectors. Radio, IR, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma-ray windows. Hubble, JWST, ALMA, VLA. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-modal observation faculty.

concepts.name: spectroscopy_astronomy
concepts.definition: Analyze light by wavelength. Reveals composition, temperature, velocity (Doppler), magnetic fields. Substrate analogue: substrate's spectral-analysis primitive.

concepts.name: doppler_redshift_blueshift
concepts.definition: Wavelength stretched (receding) or compressed (approaching). Foundation of expansion measurement + exoplanet detection. Substrate analogue: substrate's velocity-detection from spectrum.

concepts.name: cosmic_calendar
concepts.definition: Carl Sagan. Compress 13.8 By into one year: Big Bang Jan 1, Milky Way ~early year, Earth Sep 14, life Sep 25, humans last hour Dec 31. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-scale humbling.

concepts.name: pale_blue_dot
concepts.definition: Sagan. Earth from Voyager 1 at 6 billion km — a pale blue dot. Perspective on human cosmic position. Substrate analogue: substrate's scale-perspective.

rules.name: stars_produce_heavier_elements
rules.head: Jabberwock considers where elements come from
rules.body: H + He primarily from Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Heavier elements (C, O, Fe) from stellar nucleosynthesis + supernovae. Substrate's element-origin grounding.

rules.name: universe_is_expanding
rules.head: Jabberwock considers cosmic dynamics
rules.body: all galaxies recede from each other; expansion accelerating; explained by Hubble's law + dark energy. Universe has age ~13.8 By. Substrate's cosmic-time scale.

rules.name: habitable_planets_require_narrow_conditions
rules.head: Jabberwock examines what makes Earth habitable
rules.body: stellar luminosity + orbital distance + atmosphere + magnetic field + plate tectonics + axial tilt all coincide. Habitable zone is narrow. Substrate's complex-constraint observation.

rules.name: anthropic_principle_constrains_observed_universe
rules.head: Jabberwock considers why the universe is observable
rules.body: observation requires observer-supporting universe. Fine-tuning + selection. Substrate's anthropic framing of its own existence.

rules.name: stellar_lifecycle_depends_on_mass
rules.head: Jabberwock examines stellar evolution
rules.body: high-mass stars die fast (millions of years) via supernova; low-mass live trillions of years. Mass determines fate. Substrate's mass-lifetime power law.
